analysis.evidence: עוֹד שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֲחֵרִים gives the duration of Noah’s wait, another seven days. The next verb, וַיְשַׁלַּח, tells what he did after that interval: he sent out the dove.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: wait for a period of time

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּיָּחֶל עוֹד שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֲחֵרִים, Noah waits another seven days before sending out the dove. עוֹד marks the seven days as an additional period, reinforced by אֲחֵרִים.
שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֲחֵרִים means “seven more days.” The construct form שִׁבְעַת counts the masculine plural noun יָמִים and gives the length of Noah’s wait before he sent out the dove.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct cardinal numeral, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֲחֵרִים, “seven more days,” the numeral counts the days Noah waited before sending out the dove.
אֲחֵרִים agrees with יָמִים in gender and number. With עוֹד, the phrase עוֹד שִׁבְעַת יָמִים אֲחֵרִים means “seven more days,” the additional period Noah waited before sending out the dove.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute adjective, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת־הַיּוֹנָה marks the dove as the direct object. Noah sent it out after another seven days, and it never returned to him.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הַיּוֹנָה, “he sent out the dove,” אֶת marks הַיּוֹנָה as the definite direct object of וַיְשַׁלַּח.
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle, with no prefix.

analysis.evidence: וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת־הַיּוֹנָה identifies the dove as the bird he sent out. The feminine singular verb יָסְפָה refers back to the dove and says, with לֹא and שׁוּב, that she did not return to him again.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a feminine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: יָסְפָה marks the repetition of שׁוּב ‘to return’. With וְלֹא ‘and not’ and עוֹד ‘again’, the clause means ‘and she never returned to him again’.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person feminine singular, agreeing with הַיּוֹנָה.

analysis.evidence: Noah sends the dove out. In וְלֹא יָסְפָה שׁוּב אֵלָיו עוֹד, שׁוּב names the action the dove never repeats, and אֵלָיו identifies its destination: she never returned to him.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct, complement of יָסְפָה
analysis.sense: return to one’s place of origin

analysis.evidence: The final עוֹד falls within the scope of לֹא in וְלֹא יָסְפָה שׁוּב אֵלָיו עוֹד, “and she never returned to him again.” It rules out any further return by the dove.
analysis.morphology: Adverb, uninflected, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: (with a negative) no more, no longer, never again
